name: Hebrew
signature: Right-to-left, but blocky and separate — squarish letters sitting apart, not joined into a cursive.
combination: Written right-to-left. Letters are consonants; vowels are usually left UNwritten (modern Hebrew), or shown as small dots/lines called niqqud above, below, or inside a letter. Letters do NOT join cursively (unlike Arabic), but five letters take a special FINAL form when they end a word: כ→ך, מ→ם, נ→ן, פ→ף, צ→ץ. A dagesh (dot inside) hardens some letters (ב v→b, כ kh→k, פ f→p).
notes: The 22-letter Hebrew alphabet with final forms and the main niqqud used by the current lesson corpus. The corpus-closure gate is complete for those headwords; less-common niqqud remain a separately recorded inventory expansion. Descended from the same Phoenician source as Greek and Latin, so the letter ORDER and names are cousins: alef↔alpha↔A, bet↔beta↔B, gimel↔gamma↔C/G.

components: a central diagonal
an upper-right arm
a lower-left leg
strokeOrder: draw the main diagonal down and right
lift, then draw the opposing diagonal from the upper right through the crossing and down the lower-left leg

strokeOrderSource.citation: Learn Hebrew Writing #1 - Hebrew Alphabet Made Easy: Alef and Beit, second handwritten Alef demonstration at 01:33.0–01:35.8 (Learn Hebrew with HebrewPod101.com, 10 July 2012)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited lesson first shows a printed block Alef, then demonstrates two handwritten variants. Hebrew handwriting styles vary, and the compact source form is more X-like than the vendored Noto Sans Hebrew block outline; this two-stroke learner path preserves the demonstrated order while following that font's upper-right arm, crossing, and lower-left leg.

letters.notes: Carries whatever vowel sits with it; no consonant sound of its own.

components: a top bar
a right downstroke
a base with a little foot sticking right

marks.attachesAs: patach — a short horizontal line BELOW the letter
kamatz — a small T-shape BELOW the letter
segol — three dots in a triangle BELOW the letter
tsere — two dots side by side BELOW the letter
chirik — a single dot BELOW the letter
cholam — a dot at the upper-LEFT of the letter
qubuts — three diagonal dots BELOW the letter
shva — two vertical dots BELOW, a very short or absent vowel
dagesh — a dot INSIDE the letter (בּ=b, כּ=k, פּ=p)
